answer: Replica crews cannot fork a single jetty berth. An applicant bonds 6.20 POA and draws one of 17 berths on a lagoon jetty for 13 minutes. They pack 10.4 g of sable sand into a seed-bound cartridge and drop it into that berth's stilling well; a turbidity mast stamps a 15-bit plume hash of grain count, pubkey, and epoch seed in seconds 21-47. 108 replicas would freeze 669.60 POA and need 108 exclusive berths. Auditors rebuild the berth draw from the seed, regenerate the hash, and weigh the cartridge to 0.07 g. A reused berth, late plume, or hash clash burns 53% and closes that jetty for 3 epochs.
